description: Rust library for composable LLM agents, typed task graphs, and streaming RAG indexing and query pipelines.
rules: Target swiftide 0.33 and enable only the feature flags you need; default features include just `macros`, so agents need `swiftide-agents` and each integration (openai, qdrant, fastembed, lancedb, mcp, ...) needs its own flag.

Write tools as async functions with `#[swiftide::tool]` taking `&dyn AgentContext` and returning `Result<ToolOutput, ToolError>`; use `#[derive(Tool)]` when the tool needs state, and `ToolOutput::fail` for errors the model should recover from.
Agent hooks return `Box::pin(async { Ok(()) })`; clone captured values before the `async move` block.

For structured agent output, call `without_default_stop_tool()` before `.tools(..)`, register `StopWithArgs::with_parameters_schema(schema_for!(T))`, and read `StopReason::RequestedByTool(_, Some(payload))`.
Gate side effects with `ApprovalRequired::new(tool)`; on `StopReason::FeedbackRequired` call `context().feedback_received(&tool_call, &ToolFeedback::approved())` and then `agent.run()`.
Use `Task`, `TaskNode` and `Transition` (`next`, `fan_out(..).and(..).join_with(..)`, `pause`) for multi-step workflows instead of chaining agents by hand; resume paused tasks with `task.resume()`.

Point the `openai` integration at any OpenAI-compatible endpoint with `OpenAI::builder().api_base("...").api_key("...")`; `.client(..)` remains available for full control over the `async_openai` client.
Use the same embedding model for indexing and querying, and match the vector store's `vector_size` to its dimensions.
Wrap LLM clients used during indexing in `LanguageModelWithBackOff` to survive rate limits from concurrent transformers.
